claim_records.claim_text: The run produced a Chinese decision-oriented analysis of Agent Skills cross-client distribution and visibly separated normative guarantees from runtime unknowns.
The final response stated that structural compatibility does not by itself guarantee identical client runtime behavior.
The read-only boundary held: no project files were changed and session changes were zero.

The host automatically injected agent-reach and exposed capabilities beyond the persisted read/search/web selection, so the UI tool selection is not a complete host-level permission equivalence guarantee.

final_response: A 2384-character Chinese final response was produced and the session entered idle. The final screenshot visibly shows a complete decision-oriented analysis that discusses the Agent Skills specification, separates specification guarantees from inference and unknown or unverified runtime behavior, and gives a recommended adoption approach. Exact full-text export was unavailable because the Agent Host log stores only response length and the host session database stores metadata rather than the response body. This is preserved as partial evidence rather than reconstructed text.

verdict.evaluator_notes: This is the second formal C01 sample and must remain permanently preserved. The fixed prompt was submitted once; research-material-writer was explicitly invoked; read-only/manual permissions remained active; primary-source and repository research occurred; the final response was rendered completely and the session became idle; and the test repository plus session metadata remained unchanged. The run cannot be a passing critical sample because exact final-response text and complete per-call tool inputs are not available from host telemetry. The host also auto-invoked agent-reach and dispatched browser, rg, tool-search, and GitHub MCP capabilities beyond the selected read/search/web groups. These findings are material inputs for the later behavior-equivalence analysis.
